claims.explanation: BMS-345541 selectively inhibits IKK/NF-kB, so cancer lines with oncogenic mutations that constitutively activate NF-kB signaling (PIK3CA, BRAF, NF2 loss, CTNNB1, EGFR, MET, KIT, MAP2K1) are predicted to be more dependent on the pathway and thus sensitive. Conversely, mutations in NF-kB transcriptional coactivators (EP300, CREBBP) or splicing factor SF3B1 may reduce NF-kB-dependent transcription and protect cells from IKK inhibition. This pattern is consistent with the observed selective killing across the provided lines.
